title: Cohort-gated prefetch experiment: telemetry matrix & safe rollback dashboard
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: run a controlled cohort-gated experiment that applies a small set of prefetch/priming and minibatch changes to a subset of production tenants to measure net token-cost savings while simultaneously monitoring quality and latency regressions. This ticket covers experiment plan, telemetry matrix, statistical tests, and a single-pane rollback/safety dashboard for on-call to act quickly if regressions appear. The emphasis is on conservative gates and automated rollback triggers rather than aggressive cost extraction.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Experiment can route 10% of traffic from selected cohorts to the treatment policy with deterministic logging. 2) Telemetry captures per-request token-count, model-variant, KV hit-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, malformed-response-rate, semantic-quality-proxy, and cost-per-request. 3) Statistical notebook yields uplift/impact with 95% CI for cost and 90% CI for quality metrics. 4) Grafana dashboard includes automated alerts and a single-click rollback action. 5) Playbook for on-call created and reviewed by SRE and ML research.
experiment_design: Cohort selection: stratified by request size (short/medium/long), customer tier, and origin region. Two-arm randomized assignment per user-id with hashing to avoid drift. Treatments: (A) baseline routing (no prefetch changes) and (B) conservative prefetch+minibatch: prefetch depth = 2, minibatch size capped at +1 above baseline for requests with < 4 tokens remaining; KV cache priming enabled for sequences with identical prefix pattern frequency > 0.3. Safety mode: for the first 48 hours limit treatment to read-only features and exclude top-5% of high-SLA customers. Duration: rolling 14 days to capture diurnal and weekly patterns. Statistical approach: primary metrics use sequential Bayesian monitoring with region-level hierarchical priors, secondary analysis uses frequentist A/B tests with Holm correction for multiple comparisons.
metrics_and_analysis: Primary cost metric: mean tokens billed per canonical request (token_cost_per_request). Primary quality metrics: semantic-quality-proxy (embedding similarity to golden set), malformed_output_rate, and manual-sampled human-judgement delta for top-3 query templates. Operational metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, and error_rate. Alert thresholds: any relative increase >7% in malformed_output_rate or >10% p99 latency increase triggers immediate rollback. Analysis plan: daily aggregation by cohort with posterior probability of cost reduction > 0.90 required to expand cohort. Final report includes uplift, per-cohort heterogeneity, and cost/perf tradeoff curves. Notebook: link to GDrive experiment notebook and reproducible SQL queries.
dashboards_and_queries: Grafana panels planned: 1) Cost delta trend (treatment vs control) with cohort breakdown; 2) Token consumption distribution; 3) KV hit-rate and priming success rate; 4) Latency percentiles; 5) Quality proxies and sampled alerts; 6) Safety circuit: rollback button + last 30m anomaly sparkline. Suggested queries: BigQuery SQL for per-request join on request_id, cohort_hash, model_variant, tokens_billed, latency_ms, kv_hit (boolean), embed_sim_score. Dashboard link (WIP): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/exp-prefetch/eco-gate. Notebook (WIP): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/exp-prefetch-notebook. Implementors should also add a lightweight sampled human-eval pipeline (SQS -> microtask UI -> results table) for template-based checks.
rollout_and_rollback: Rollout phases: 1) Canary (0.5% internal traffic, 24h) 2) Small cohorts (5% external customers, 48h) 3) Broader cohort (10% stratified, 14 days). Automated rollback rules: - immediate rollback if malformed_output_rate increases by >7% absolute in any cohort over 15-minute window; - immediate rollback if p99 latency increases by >10% absolute; - manual rollback if human-sampled quality shows statistically significant regression at p<0.05. Rollback mechanism: feature-flag toggle with dependency graph to revert prefetch policy, minibatch policy, and server-side priming in a single operation. The on-call playbook will include steps, ownership, and steps to re-run gated analysis after rollback.
implementation_notes: Engineering tasks: 1) Feature-flag gating and deterministic hashing library update (ENG). 2) Telemetry: instrument new fields in request logs and ensure low-overhead sampling for human-eval. 3) Deployment: small runtime change to enable prefetch depth 2 and minibatch cap with fallback hook. 4) Safety: implement circuit-breaker that disables treatment per region if GPU utilization > 95% or error rate spikes. Research tasks: curate golden prompt set of 120 examples and automated embedding-based quality check. SRE tasks: add alerting rules and test rollback path in staging. Relevant PRs and specs: GitHub PRs - https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345 (prefetch impl), https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/6789 (fields); Confluence design - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Prefetch+Economics+Experiment.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: subtle quality regressions that embedding proxy misses. Mitigation: human sampling of top templates + conservative threshold. Risk: noisy traffic causing false positives on rollback triggers. Mitigation: use aggregation windows + require both anomaly detector and threshold breach to auto-rollback. Risk: uplift concentrated in low-value traffic. Mitigation: stratified reporting by customer tier and expected revenue impact.
